detector._note: Keypoints 23-11-13 / 24-12-14 (hip-shoulder-elbow), 3D world angle. Arms hang in the 16-25 band and a correct raise turns in the 90-110 band. Past 110 the shoulder stops abducting and starts pressing, which is a different movement and is not counted.

stage._note: Specified by the player, 6 Sep 2026: arms down in a 16-25 band, the raise counts above 90, and it is refused past 110. countAt RETURN makes this a whole-cycle rule, so the rep lands on the way down rather than on the way up, which is also the only way the ceiling can mean anything: how far you went is not known until you turn around. rest was < 20 for one build and that alone broke the exercise. Captured from the player's own phone the same night (2710 frames with the arms down): only 26 percent of them read under 20 on both arms at once, and after a raise it took up to 20 SECONDS for a qualifying frame to appear. Under 25 it is 58 percent and at most 1.8 seconds. In RETURN mode the rep can only land on a resting frame, so an unreachable rest threshold does not make counting strict, it makes it silent. plane > 0.5 is the fix for front raises counting as lateral ones. The hip-shoulder-elbow angle is the same whether the arm goes out to the side or straight out in front, so the angle alone cannot tell the two apart; this asks the upper arm to be within 60 degrees of straight out to the side. Measured on traces/reference-lateral-raise.jsonl: a correct raise reads 0.62 to 1.00 sideways at the top (median 0.84) and a front raise reads about 0. On the player's own phone it read 0.95 at the quartile.

tempo._note: measured window: topExit crossing -> bottomEnter crossing, not the full descent

cues.enter: Face the camera, arms hanging at your sides (16-25 degrees).
cues.tooHigh: Raise the arms out to the sides, not out in front, to about 100 degrees.
cues.framing: I can't see your hips — step back.
